title: Stable softmax composition
summary: NumPy has no dedicated softmax API; this small composition subtracts the maximum, exponentiates, then normalizes by the row sum.
formula: softmax(x)ᵢ = exp(xᵢ − max(x)) / Σⱼ exp(xⱼ − max(x))
example:
import numpy as np

x = np.array([1, 2, 3, 4], dtype=np.float32)
shifted = x - np.max(x, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
exponentials = np.exp(shifted)
probabilities = exponentials / np.sum(exponentials, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
limitations: This is a stable educational softmax composition, not a built-in numpy.softmax API.
The fixture is one four-value vector; multidimensional axes, masks, special dtypes, and backward gradients are omitted.

tensors.name: probabilities
tensors.description: Exponentials normalized to sum to one.

stages.title: Stabilize and exponentiate
stages.summary: Subtract the maximum logit before exponentiation, then compute one exponential per element.
stages.insight: The maximum shift changes no normalized probabilities and avoids unnecessary overflow.

stages.title: Normalize by the sum
stages.summary: Accumulate the exponential denominator, then divide each exponential by that shared total.
stages.insight: The output is a probability distribution whose values sum to one.
